post_title: What will be the seasonally adjusted month-on-month percentage change in New Zealand's total electronic card transaction values for October 2026 (Stats NZ, released 12 November 2026)?

question.title: What will be the seasonally adjusted month-on-month percentage change in New Zealand's total electronic card transaction values for October 2026 (Stats NZ, released 12 November 2026)?
question.description:
Electronic card transactions (ECT) is a monthly Stats NZ series covering debit, credit, and charge card transactions with New Zealand-based merchants, both card-present and card-not-present. Values are GST-inclusive, at the national level, and are not adjusted for price changes. Stats NZ publishes actual, seasonally adjusted, and trend values for three aggregations — total (all industries), retail industries, and core retail industries — producing the seasonally adjusted and trend series with X-13ARIMA-SEATS. Releases are published mid-month at 10:45am, and Stats NZ describes the series as an indicator of changes in consumer spending and economic activity.

This question concerns the next release, "Electronic card transactions: October 2026", scheduled for 12 November 2026 at 10:45am NZDT; the September 2026 release (https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/electronic-card-transactions-september-2026/) states: "Next release: Electronic card transactions: October 2026 will be released on 12 November 2026."

Latest data (September 2026, published 16 October 2026): the seasonally adjusted total value of electronic card spending, including the two non-retail categories (services and other non-retail), decreased from August 2026, down $51 million (0.5 percent). Retail industry card spending fell 0.4 percent ($30 million) and core retail fell 0.7 percent ($41 million); at industry level, fuel spending rose 2.9 percent ($15 million) while hospitality fell 2.3 percent ($33 million). In actual terms, cardholders made 167 million transactions across all industries in September 2026, with a total actual value of $9.2 billion and an average value of $55 per transaction.

Reported monthly changes in the seasonally adjusted total (all industries) series during 2026 include: January −0.7 percent (−$70 million), April −1.6 percent (−$160 million), May +2.2 percent (+$212 million), July +1.0 percent (+$94 million), and September −0.5 percent (−$51 million). Monthly moves have therefore generally fallen in a range of roughly −1.6 to +2.2 percent, with increases and decreases both common and no strong recent trend.

Context for October 2026: annual CPI inflation was 3.7 percent in the 12 months to September 2026, with quarterly CPI up 0.7 percent and petrol prices up 19.1 percent over the year (https://www.stats.govt.nz/news/annual-inflation-at-3-7-percent-in-september-2026/); September 2026 food prices were flat month on month with annual food price inflation of 2.4 percent. Official October price data ("Selected price indexes: October 2026", which includes food and fuel prices) is not published until 17 November 2026 — after this question resolves — and the Reserve Bank's credit card spending series is next released on 20 November 2026, so forecasters will not have official October spending or price data at resolution and must rely on weekly fuel-price monitoring, news reporting, and other partial indicators. October 2026 contains five Saturdays and includes Labour Day on Monday 26 October 2026, both of which affect unadjusted spending patterns.

question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to the seasonally adjusted month-on-month percentage change in the total value of electronic card transactions (all industries, i.e. including the services and other non-retail categories) for October 2026, as reported in Stats NZ's information release "Electronic card transactions: October 2026", published on 12 November 2026 at 10:45am NZDT and listed at https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/.

The resolving figure is the percentage Stats NZ states in that release for the change in the seasonally adjusted total value of electronic card spending — the figure in the sentence of the form "the total value of electronic card spending, including the two non-retail categories (services and other non-retail), [increased/decreased] from September 2026, up/down $X million (Y percent)". For example, the September 2026 release reported "down $51 million (0.5 percent)", which corresponds to -0.5.

If the October 2026 release does not state a percentage for the total (all industries) series, the question instead resolves to the percentage change between the seasonally adjusted total values for September 2026 and October 2026 published in that release.
question.fine_print: Resolution uses the figures as first published in the release of 12 November 2026; later revisions to seasonally adjusted levels do not change the answer. If that release is delayed, resolution waits until it is published.
